title: Orchestration and resiliency for scheduled customer usage exports (CSV + S3 + webhooks)
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Goal: Replace the current ad-hoc export runners with a hardened orchestration service that reliably produces scheduled customer usage exports (CSV and newline-delimited JSON for large exports), deposits artifacts to S3 (either per-customer buckets or a shared bucket with strong prefixes), and/or delivers a manifest to configured webhook endpoints. The service must:

- Provide idempotent, resumable exports so long-running exports survive scheduler/node restarts.
- Support export schemas versioning and include an atomic manifest.json with schema_version and checksums.
- Enforce per-customer throttles and concurrency limits to avoid overloading downstream billing and analytics pipelines.
- Implement robust webhook delivery with exponential backoff, jitter, and DLQ for permanent failures; support signed webhook payloads and replay protection.
- Emit detailed metrics: export_request_count, export_success_count, export_fail_count, export_latency_ms_p50/p95/p99, export_bytes_total, webhook_retry_attempts, manifest_generation_duration.
- Make exports listable and auditable in the Console: status, size, duration, delivery target, signed URL (if applicable), and audit log entries for who requested the export.

Design decisions: per-customer S3 buckets provide the strongest tenant isolation and straightforward KMS key scoping. Trade-offs: provisioning buckets for every new customer increases account management complexity; alternatively a shared bucket with path-level separation is cheaper but requires stricter prefix ACLs and extra audit metadata. For initial rollout we will support a hybrid model: existing enterprise customers get per-customer buckets (provisioned on demand during onboarding) and all other customers use a shared bucket with enforced prefix ACLs.

Data pipeline/backpressure interactions: the orchestration service will push completed export manifests to the analytics shipper (internal stream) which will enforce downstream ingestion batching. The orchestrator will also track export checkpoints (offsets) for large streaming exports so partial files can be resumed and retries avoid reprocessing the entire dataset.

Failure handling: in-flight export failures are retried locally with exponential backoff (max 6 attempts). If delivery to webhook or S3 continues to fail, the export transitions to "error: retryable" with an entry in the DLQ topic and a PagerDuty alert if the customer is enterprise-tier. Operators can replay DLQ messages via tooling in the Console or via a cli repair command.

Migration plan: phase 1 (canary customers) -> phase 2 (all enterprise) -> phase 3 (all customers). We'll run parallel exports for 2 weeks and a checksum compare against the legacy exporter to validate parity. Rollback plan: ability to re-enable legacy runner per-customer if a regression is detected.

Security/compliance: all S3 objects are encrypted with KMS. Exports with PII flags require additional approval and must be restricted to per-customer buckets only. Audit logs for export requests and downloads will be shipped to the central audit store for 7 years (configurable).
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler can enqueue and start exports for a customer on a configured cron and adhoc requests from Console/CLI/API
Exports are idempotent and resumable: an interrupted export restarts from last checkpoint and produces identical output (same manifest checksum)
Webhook delivery implements retry/backoff and dead-lettering; failed webhook deliveries are visible in Console with next-retry timestamp
Per-customer concurrency and bandwidth limits are enforced and configurable via Console settings
Signed URLs for completed artifacts are generated with configurable TTLs and require role-based permissions to reveal
Monitoring dashboard created with the metrics listed in the description and alerts for export_success_rate < 98% over 15m and median export latency regressions
Migration verification run shows parity with legacy exporter for canary set (checksums match)
